 --> Karwa Chauth 2026 date and time: When will the Moon rise on October 29? Check puja muhurat, fasting timings and when you can break your fast
 Karwa Chauth 2026 falls on October 29. Check the moonrise time, puja muhurat, fasting hours, Chaturthi Tithi and when married women can break their fast.

 Karwa Chauth 2026 date and time: When will the Moon rise on October 29? Check puja muhurat, fasting timings and when you can break your fast (image: canva) Karwa Chauth 2026 is on October 29.
 Puja muhurat is from 5:43 PM to 6:57 PM.
 Expected moonrise is at 8:44 PM in Chennai.

 Karwa Chauth 2026 will be observed on Thursday, October 29, when married Hindu women across India will observe a day-long fast and pray for their husbands' long life, good health and well-being. From the early-morning start of the fast to the evening puja and the much-awaited moon sighting, knowing the correct timings can help women plan their rituals and celebrations.
 According to Drik Panchang, the Karwa Chauth puja muhurat will be from 5:43 PM to 6:57 PM, while the expected moonrise is at 8:44 PM in Chennai. The fasting period is listed as running from 6:02 AM to 8:44 PM. However, moonrise and auspicious puja timings can vary by city, so women should check the timings for their location before beginning the rituals.
 Karwa Chauth 2026: Date and important timings 
 Karwa Chauth falls on Krishna Paksha Chaturthi, the fourth day of the waning lunar phase. The festival is widely observed in North India and is also known as Karak Chaturthi. Here are the key timings for Karwa Chauth 2026, according to Drik Panchang:
 Festival Date and Time  
 Karwa Chauth Thursday, October 29, 2026 
 Chaturthi Tithi Begins 1:06 AM, October 29 
 Chaturthi Tithi Ends 10:09 PM, October 29 
 Karwa Chauth Puja Muhurat 5:43 PM to 6:57 PM 
 Fasting Time 6:02 AM to 8:44 PM 
 Expected Moonrise 8:44 PM 
 Puja Muhurat Duration 1 hour 14 minutes 
 Fasting Duration 14 hours 42 minutes 
 Important: The moonrise time and puja muhurat may differ in Delhi, Mumbai, Lucknow, Jaipur and other cities. Check your local Panchang for location-specific timings. 
 When will the Moon rise on Karwa Chauth 2026? 
 The moon is expected to rise at 8:44 PM on October 29, according to Drik Panchang. Moonrise is one of the most significant moments of Karwa Chauth because it marks the end of the traditional fast. Women generally wait for the moon to become visible before performing the evening rituals. They offer arghya, or water, to the moon and pray for their husbands' health, longevity and prosperity. Many women then look at the moon through a sieve, followed by looking at their husbands through the same sieve.
 In many households, the husband offers his wife water and food to help her break the fast. The exact sequence of rituals may differ according to family traditions and regional customs.
 Since the moon does not rise at the same time everywhere, women should avoid relying on a single nationwide moonrise time. Local weather conditions can also affect visibility, even when the astronomical moonrise time is known.
 Karwa Chauth puja muhurat 2026 
 The Karwa Chauth puja muhurat will begin at 5:43 PM and end at 6:57 PM, giving devotees one hour and 14 minutes for the evening worship, according to the timings listed by Drik Panchang.
 During the puja, women worship Goddess Parvati, Lord Shiva, Lord Ganesha and other members of Shiva's family. Prayers are offered for the well-being and long life of their husbands. The rituals may include listening to the Karwa Chauth vrat katha, preparing the puja thali and using a traditional earthen pot called a karwa.
 Women often dress in festive clothing, wear bangles and apply mehendi as part of the day's celebrations. In many families, the evening puja is performed collectively, allowing women to gather and follow traditional customs together.
 The puja muhurat is distinct from the moonrise time. Completing the evening worship does not, by itself, mean the fast has ended. Women who observe the traditional fast generally wait until the moon is sighted and the prescribed moon-worship rituals are completed.
 Karwa Chauth fasting timings: When does the fast begin and end? 
 Traditionally, women begin their fast before sunrise and abstain from food and water until the moon is sighted at night. Many families begin the day with sargi, a pre-dawn meal that is commonly prepared or given by the mother-in-law. It may include fruits, sweets, dry fruits and other foods, depending on family customs.
 After sunrise, women who follow the strict traditional fast avoid eating or drinking until the evening rituals are complete. However, practices vary, and individuals may follow different arrangements based on their health, family traditions and personal circumstances.
 The listed fasting end time should not be treated as a universal time for every city. Since moonrise varies geographically, women should follow the local timing and their customary rituals when deciding when to break the fast.
 Why is Karwa Chauth celebrated? 
 Karwa Chauth is traditionally observed by married Hindu women who pray for their husbands' long life, health and prosperity. The festival holds particular significance in North Indian states, where it is marked by fasting, worship and family gatherings. The observance falls on Krishna Paksha Chaturthi in the Hindu lunar month of Kartik. Under the Amanta calendar followed in parts of western and southern India, the month may be referred to as Ashwin. Despite this difference in the naming of the lunar month, Karwa Chauth is observed on the same day.
 The festival also coincides with Sankashti Chaturthi, a fasting observance dedicated to Lord Ganesha. In Maharashtra and some other regions, devotees may observe a form of Sankashti Chaturthi associated with Vakratunda, a form of Lord Ganesha.
 What is the significance of the Karwa or Karak Pot? 
 Karwa Chauth is also known as Karak Chaturthi. The word karwa or karak refers to the earthen pot traditionally used to hold water for the moon offering, known as arghya. The pot plays an important role in the evening puja and is often included in the puja thali along with other ritual items. In some traditions, the karwa is also offered as daan, or a religious gift, according to customary practices.
 The moon offering is an important part of the observance, as it marks the completion of the day's fast for women who follow the traditional ritual.
 What comes after Karwa Chauth?  
 Ahoi Ashtami is observed four days after Karwa Chauth in the Hindu lunar calendar. The festival is associated with prayers for children's well-being and is traditionally observed by many women, particularly in North India, for the health and longevity of their sons. While Karwa Chauth focuses on prayers for husbands, Ahoi Ashtami has a different religious significance. Both observances remain part of the wider calendar of Hindu festivals and fasting traditions.
 As Karwa Chauth 2026 approaches, women can prepare by checking their city's moonrise time, arranging the items needed for the evening puja and confirming the local muhurat. For those observing the traditional fast, the moon sighting remains the moment they will be waiting for throughout the day.
